summary.summary: Covering report presenting the draft Annual Governance Statement for 2025/26 (the AGS itself is Appendix 1, a separate document). Two points matter for a lender. First, the draft AGS has been published alongside the council's draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, with the final versions due by the 31 January 2027 statutory deadline after a further update in October 2026 — the reporting cycle is on its statutory track. Second, the council says no NEW significant governance issues have arisen since the final 2024/25 AGS was approved in February 2026, but the existing ones continue: the draft focuses on updating progress on financial sustainability, improvement and transformation, governance and internal control, leadership capacity, children's services improvement and partnership working. In short, a council still working through a known list of significant issues, with no fresh deterioration disclosed and no figures in this paper.

signals.headline: Draft AGS 2025/26 published alongside the draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, in line with statutory requirements; final accountability statements due by the 31 January 2027 backstop after an October 2026 committee update
signals.why: The unaudited 2025/26 balance sheet is now public and the governance disclosures around it are on the statutory timetable rather than slipping.

compliance.notes: High-quality, Arlingclose-advised strategy: strongest areas are the liability benchmark (charted to the end of the debt profile with all balances and assumptions), the full prudential-indicator suite, the capital strategy/MRP and a comprehensive investment strategy covering the council's ~£60m of service/commercial investments. Weakest areas are formal governance artefacts not restated in the annual documents (no explicit adoption of the TM Code's four clauses; no audit-qualification flag; no explicit sterling-only borrowing statement or paras 51-53 compliance statement; no formal IMPs), and, for a commercial investor, no quantified commercial/service-income dependence ratio. Note: the packet's capital_strategy.url (s134122) was a 2027/28 MTFS-assumptions Cabinet paper with no capital-strategy content; the real Capital/Investment strategies and prudential indicators were read from the MTFS 2026-2030 full report (Annexes 5, 6, B, C). The packet TMSS url (s131504) was a cover report; the real TMSS is Annex 7 (s131505).

Annex 6 paras 6.46-6.47 (Prudential Code changes / government opposition to commercial property referenced), 6.69 (guidance followed)
Annex 6 paras 6.31, 6.54, 6.63: security/liquidity/risk-assessment set out per investment category
TMSS para 7.31 approved borrowing sources are all UK-based (PWLB, UK public sector, UK-authorised banks, National Wealth Fund)

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East audit committee asks for quarterly reports on delivery against ministers' expectations
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council's Audit and Governance Committee has asked for quarterly assurance reports on how the council is meeting the expectations set by ministers. The request is recorded in the committee's action log for its meeting on 15 October 2026. Reporting is to begin at the next appropriate meeting.

The log says the reports should focus on "material exceptions, changes in risk, delivery against ministerial expectations and evidence that improvement is embedded and sustained." They are also to include evidence of organisational and cultural change, among them staff survey results and measures of whether improvement has lasted.

The papers describe the council as subject to a Best Value Notice, a formal government notice about how the council runs its services and money. The action log gives no figures, dates for the notice, or details of what ministers have asked for.
news_drafts.paper_title: Audit and Governance Committee Action Log - October 2026

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East balances 2026/27 forecast using £24.995m of exceptional financial support, about 5% of budget
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council has reached a balanced forecast for 2026/27 only through the planned use of £24.995m of exceptional financial support, according to a minute extract from its Cabinet considered in the papers for the full Council meeting on 14 October 2026. Exceptional financial support is government permission to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending, and is a last resort.

The sum is roughly 5% of the council's net service budget of around £450m. The minute says the balanced position was "achieved through the planned use of £24.995m of Exceptional Financial Support". The paper records that, despite the balanced forecast, Cabinet noted the continued fragility of the council's financial resilience.

The extract comes from the Cabinet's handling of supplementary revenue requests, which are requests for extra day-to-day spending authority during the year. The material before the desk does not set out which services the money supports, how the support will be financed, or what the council plans to do to reduce its reliance on it in later years.

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East Cabinet told Exceptional Financial Support is "not sustainable in the medium to long term"
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council used exceptional financial support for 2026/27 and expects to need it in future years, according to the budget and medium-term financial strategy update before its Cabinet on 8 October 2026. Exceptional financial support is permission from government to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending, and is a last resort. The paper calls it a temporary emergency measure rather than a financial solution, and says: "This is not sustainable in the medium to long term and needs to be addressed urgently for the Council to be financially sustainable."

The medium-term financial strategy is the council's plan for the next three to five years, showing the gap between what it expects to spend and what it expects to have. The paper's second table sets out the funding shortfalls that remain once the council's normal sources of income are used up. The extract supplied gives no figures for those shortfalls.

The council's Audit and Governance Committee met on 5 October. Its minutes describe a review by CIPFA, the public finance accountancy body, commissioned as part of the council's response to a Best Value Notice, a government intervention, and its application for exceptional financial support. The committee asked the council's chief finance officer to report any material deterioration in financial resilience, reserves, savings, benefits from transformation work, exit from the support, or balance-sheet risk, through the council's existing financial monitoring and statutory reporting.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Annual Report
findings.headline: Alternative Service Delivery Vehicle governance significant issue resolved and removed from Annual Governance Statement
findings.detail: ASDV governance was flagged as a significant issue in the 2024/25 AGS draft. The Committee approved its removal from the final AGS in February 2026, confirming the underlying governance issue had been resolved.
findings.matters: Resolution of a previously identified significant governance issue demonstrates the council has addressed a control weakness; removal from the AGS signals the issue is no longer material.
findings.quote: The Committee also approved the removal of the ASDV Governance significant issue from future versions of the AGS.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Annual Report
findings.headline: Council identified significant financial pressures; financial sustainability is 2026/27 governance priority
findings.detail: The Chair noted the Council is tackling significant financial pressures through its transformation journey. For 2026/27, the Committee identified Financial Sustainability and Financial Governance as a strategic priority, with emphasis on budget management, savings delivery, financial resilience and governance arrangements supporting the medium-term financial strategy.
findings.matters: A council explicitly identifying significant financial pressures signals budget stress; the governance committee's focus on savings delivery and financial resilience indicates substantive financial management challenges ahead.
findings.quote: the Council continues to tackle the significant financial pressures through its transformation journey

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Annual Report
findings.headline: Officer Decision Records audit resulted in limited assurance opinion
findings.detail: The Committee received a detailed briefing in December 2025 on findings from an internal audit review of Officer Decision Records, which resulted in a limited assurance opinion. This indicates control gaps in governance over officer decision-making and record-keeping.
findings.matters: Officer decision records are key governance controls; limited assurance suggests the council may lack adequate documentation and oversight of how significant decisions are made.
findings.quote: the Committee also received a detailed briefing in December 2025 on the findings of the Officer Decision Records audit review, which resulted in a limited assurance opinion

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Annual Report
findings.headline: 2024/25 final accounts not signed off until February 2026, nine months after year end
findings.detail: In June 2025 the Committee noted accounts publication had been delayed and would be 31 July 2025. The final accounts were not received until February 2026, extending the timeline well beyond the statutory backstop date and following similar delays with 2023/24 accounts.
findings.matters: Delayed year-end accounts indicate underlying financial reporting or governance challenges; extended delays beyond the backstop date signal particular difficulties in preparing or auditing accounts that affect a lender's assessment of financial governance.
findings.figures: 31 March 2025 year end to February 2026 accounts received
findings.quote: The Committee received the final Statement of Accounts along with the external auditor's Audit of Accounts report for the year 2024/25 in February 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Annual Report
findings.headline: Limited assurance rating given for overall governance, risk management and control framework in 2024/25
findings.detail: The Head of Audit, Risk & Assurance's 2024/25 Annual Opinion, received by Committee in July 2025, concluded that Limited Assurance could be provided on the adequacy and effectiveness of the Council's governance, risk management and control framework.
findings.matters: A council with limited assurance on its overall control framework poses heightened risk; this rating indicates systemic governance and control gaps that may affect service delivery, financial management and resilience.
findings.quote: The Committee also considered the 2024/25 Annual Opinion of the Head of Audit, Risk & Assurance at its July 2025 meeting which concluded that Limited Assurance could be provided on the adequacy and effectiveness of the Council's governance, risk management and control framework.

daily_post.headline: Section 151 Officer required to report any material deterioration in financial resilience, reserves, savings, transformation benefits, and EFS exit arrangements
daily_post.lead: This escalation requirement reflects formal concern about potential further financial deterioration; it establishes the council's commitment to transparent reporting of material changes to a lender.
